stories.body: A Russian aerial attack on two civilian buses in the frontline city of Kramatorsk, in Ukraine's Donetsk region, killed at least 30 people and wounded 18, according to regional authorities. Officials said one bus was directly hit and another caught fire near a dental clinic, while images showed bodies and debris on the street. The strike came amid a sharp escalation of Russian attacks that has increased civilian casualties across Ukraine; Kyiv is again urging partners to bolster air defences.
stories.headline: Russian strike on buses in Kramatorsk kills at least 30 people

stories.body: Eritrean troops have reportedly deployed in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region as renewed fighting between the Tigray People's Liberation Front and federal forces threatens to widen into a regional conflict. The violence, which resumed on 23 September, has shattered the fragile peace established after the 2020-22 civil war. Witnesses also report that armed groups are forcibly recruiting men and boys, including teenagers, while civilians try to flee the region.
stories.headline: Eritrean troops reportedly enter Ethiopia's Tigray region, raising fears of wider war

stories.body: Yemen's Houthi rebels said they launched another ballistic missile at Riyadh airport as fighting with the Saudi-led coalition continued. Saudi authorities said earlier Houthi attacks on airports in Riyadh and Abha had killed three civilians and wounded 36, while the coalition said it retaliated by striking 82 Houthi military targets. Explosions were reported in the Saudi capital on Thursday.
stories.headline: Fighting escalates in Yemen as Houthis claim another attack on Riyadh airport

stories.body: The UN's World Meteorological Organization said El Niño is expected to intensify before peaking in December and could rank among the strongest episodes recorded since at least 1950. The weather pattern is set to raise temperatures across much of the world, adding to the effects of human-driven climate change.
stories.headline: UN warns El Niño could become one of the strongest since 1950

stories.body: Canadian poet, essayist and translator Anne Carson has won the Nobel Prize in Literature for what the Swedish Academy called her bold and inventive body of work, which engages playfully with the classical tradition and creates new contemporary forms. Carson, 76, is known for writing across poetry, prose, fiction, criticism and translation, including Autobiography of Red, The Beauty of the Husband and Nox. She will receive the prize, worth 12 million Swedish kronor, in Stockholm in December.
stories.headline: Canadian poet Anne Carson wins the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature

stories.body: The FBI says it stopped an alleged ISIS-inspired plan to attack shoppers at Minnesota's Mall of America. Court records say an 18-year-old tried to buy an assault rifle with the intention of carrying out the attack.
stories.headline: FBI says it stopped an alleged ISIS-inspired planned attack at the Mall of America

stories.body: The US Supreme Court is considering an environmental challenge to an Air Force site on Guam where unexploded ordnance is destroyed. A nonprofit group argues that detonating the munitions threatens the island's main water supply, sea turtles and an Indigenous cultural site.
stories.headline: Supreme Court weighs challenge to Air Force munitions-disposal site on Guam

stories.body: The Democratic National Committee has sued the Trump administration over television ads promoting President Donald Trump's political message, alleging that they amount to illegal government propaganda. The lawsuit seeks to stop federal funding for the campaign, which AdImpact estimates has cost more than $12 million ahead of November's midterm elections.
stories.headline: DNC sues Trump administration over taxpayer-funded television ads

stories.body: Michigan Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers has called for an end to the tariff dispute with Canada in a new campaign advertisement, breaking with the Trump administration's approach weeks before the midterm elections. Rogers said Canada was not Michigan's enemy and argued that ending the dispute would help lower prices; Michigan conducts roughly $80 billion in trade with Canada annually.
stories.headline: Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers calls for an end to tariff dispute with Canada

stories.body: The death of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal after her eviction from her Madrid home has become a focal point in Spain's already heated housing debate, prompting tributes and protests in cities across the country. The case has also fuelled a political dispute before the 29 November general election: the government called her death a failure of the system, while the People's Party and Vox accused the government of exploiting it politically.
stories.headline: Death of evicted pensioner intensifies Spain's housing debate

stories.body: Spain's Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office says there are indications warranting an investigation of the PSOE for alleged bribery and influence peddling in the Leire Díez case, but considers it premature to charge the party. Prosecutors say former PSOE organisation secretary Santos Cerdán should first testify in a case examining alleged efforts to obstruct judicial and police investigations involving the party and government.
stories.headline: Anti-corruption prosecutors see evidence against PSOE in Leire Díez case but say charges are premature

stories.body: People's Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo says he will ask Spain's Central Electoral Board for additional safeguards for postal voting, after Madrid regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso urged voters not to use it. Feijóo said he trusted postal workers but not the company's former leadership, while critics within and outside the party warned that questioning the voting system could undermine confidence ahead of the 29 November election.
stories.headline: People's Party leadership joins doubts over postal voting ahead of Spain's general election

stories.body: Italy's parliament has approved a controversial electoral reform backed by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni that gives a seat bonus to a party or coalition winning at least 42% of the vote. The law allocates an additional 70 seats in the lower house and 35 in the Senate to the winning bloc, with supporters arguing it will bring stability and opponents saying it is designed to entrench Meloni's power before the 2027 election.
stories.headline: Italy approves Meloni-backed electoral reform to strengthen parliamentary majorities

stories.body: Catalonia's Rodalies commuter rail network was gradually restoring service after days of disruption caused by severe rainfall, though delays and closures persisted on several lines. Services on the R1 and R4 resumed after a further infrastructure incident, while the R2 Nord and R11 remained affected. The disruption coincided with the first day of partial strikes by Barcelona bus workers, who are seeking improved schedules, two consecutive weekly rest days and a 35-hour working week.
stories.headline: Rodalies disruptions continue after severe weather as Barcelona bus workers begin partial strikes

stories.body: Catalan authorities have issued fresh warnings for heavy rain and strong winds along the Barcelona and Girona coast after days of exceptional rainfall. Meteocat warned that some areas could receive more than 20 litres per square metre in 30 minutes, while gusts in the Empordà could exceed 90 kilometres per hour. Civil protection remains on alert as flooding, landslides and road disruptions continue, with emergency services having received thousands of weather-related calls.
stories.headline: Fresh storm warnings issued for Barcelona and Girona after days of exceptional rainfall

stories.body: Barcelona City Council and the Catalan government have reached a preliminary agreement to buy a building in Sant Andreu, suspending the eviction of about 30 residents, including six children. The purchase would use Catalonia's housing emergency fund after housing groups mobilised outside the Llenguadoc Street building. Authorities said the agreement showed the value of joint action against housing speculation, though the deal remains subject to completion.
stories.headline: Barcelona and Catalonia agree to buy Sant Andreu building to prevent eviction of 30 residents
